title: Evidencing Effectiveness to Supervisors
summary: Brings the programme together by showing how to measure, test and report the effectiveness of the financial crime framework, prepare for supervisory review and plan the next stage of AI adoption.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the programme together by showing how to measure, test and report the effectiveness of the financial crime framework, prepare for supervisory review and plan the next stage of AI adoption.
Learning Objectives: Define metrics and management information that demonstrate effectiveness
Prepare for supervisory inspections, thematic reviews and independent reviews
Produce a financial crime and AI action plan for the firm
Syllabus: Effectiveness metrics, quality assurance and board reporting
Common supervisory findings and remediation programmes
Inspection readiness: files, walkthroughs and interviews
Workshop: the firm's financial crime and AI action plan
Intended Audience: MLROs, deputy MLROs and heads of financial crime compliance
Financial crime, AML, sanctions and fraud analysts, investigators and team leaders
Compliance, risk, data and technology staff who design, validate or run financial crime systems
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Experience of AML, sanctions or fraud compliance in a regulated firm is helpful. No data science background is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)

related.title: Fraud and Scams: Prevention, Detection and Response
